hints: Focus on phases, the key test is whether the catalyst is in the same physical state as the reactants or in a different one.
In reaction 1 the reactants are gases but the iron is a solid powder, so think about what that phase difference means.
In reaction 2 both the ozone mixture and the vaporised catalyst are in the gas phase, so put the two reactions together to complete the pair.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two types of catalysis**

Homogeneous means catalyst and reactants are in the same phase. Heterogeneous means they are in different phases.

Rule to use:
$$\text{same phase = homogeneous, different phase = heterogeneous}$$

**Check reaction 1, the Haber process**

All the reactants and products are gases, but the iron catalyst is a solid.

$$\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g) \quad \text{with Fe(s)}$$ 
Solid with gases means different phases, so this is heterogeneous catalysis on the iron surface.

**Check reaction 2, ozone breakdown**

The reactants are gases and the vaporised tetrachloromethane catalyst is also a gas (it forms $\text{Cl}$ radicals in UV light).

$$2\text{O}_3(g) \rightleftharpoons 3\text{O}_2(g) \quad \text{with gaseous catalyst}$$ 
Gas with gases means the same phase, so this is homogeneous catalysis. Reaction 1 is heterogeneous and reaction 2 is homogeneous.

options.A: Incorrect. Reaction 1 is indeed heterogeneous, but reaction 2 is not. The vaporised catalyst is a gas, same phase as the gaseous ozone, so it cannot be heterogeneous.
options.B: Incorrect. Reaction 2 is indeed homogeneous, but reaction 1 is not. Solid iron with gaseous reactants is in a different phase, so it is heterogeneous, not homogeneous.
options.C: Correct. Reaction 1 has solid Fe(s) with gaseous reactants, so different phases and heterogeneous. Reaction 2 has a vaporised, gaseous catalyst with gaseous reactants, so same phase and homogeneous.
options.D: Incorrect, this is the reverse of the truth. Students who mix up the terms homogeneous (same) and heterogeneous (different) often pick this. Remember: solid plus gas is different, gas plus gas is same.
